html:
The short imperial dynasty that ruled China from 581 to 618 and joined it together again after more than 350 years of the period of division. Like the Qin before it, it unified the country, built on a vast scale, and fell fast.

It was founded by Yang Jian, known as Emperor Wen, a general from the northern military aristocracy. He took the throne of the Northern Zhou in 581 and conquered the southern Chen dynasty in 589.

What the Sui built:

  • A rebuilt capital at Chang'an, and a second planned capital at Luoyang.
  • The Grand Canal, linking the rich rice lands of the south to the north.
  • The first written examinations for state office.
  • A reformed government of departments and boards, the equal-field system of land allotment, and one standard coinage.

His son, Emperor Yang, pushed too hard. He drove millions of labourers to build canals and walls, then launched three huge failed invasions of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo between 612 and 614. Rebellions broke out across the empire. He was murdered in 618, and one of his generals, Li Yuan, founded the Tang, which inherited almost everything the Sui had built.
